network_indicators.note: No C2 URLs, IPs, sockets, or download logic were observed in static triage of either sample. MTA:SA PACKET_ID_* constants relate to the game's own protocol structures; whether the payload manipulates live traffic is Unknown (U) and needs private-server net telemetry.

decoded_string_codec.key_derivation: K is a per-decryptor constant loaded from an .rdata lane table — NOT one family key. 82 decryptor functions, one per record length; keys observed in {0x06,0x20,0x2D,0x3C,0x3F,0x40}.
decoded_string_codec.one_shot_gate: each decryptor ends with `mov byte [this+F],0` and starts with `cmp byte [this+F],0`; L = F-1 is the record length
decoded_string_codec.build_note: records are assembled on the stack from 16-byte `movaps/movups` blocks + `mov dword [ebp+d],imm32` tails, so most plaintexts (and most ciphertexts) are NOT contiguous in the file image — only 4 of 63 short records are byte-findable, which is why plain string matching cannot see them
decoded_string_codec.verification: byte-exact decodes; frozen as evidence vectors inside NrthAuditSelfTest() (21 checks)

audit_tool.name: NRTH_audit.dll / nrth_audit.exe
capabilities: wildcard pattern compile/scan (same semantics as the sample resolver 0x10002960)
read-only PE section/RVA mapping for file images and dumps
hidden-record sweep anchored on 55 8B EC / 53 8B DC
A/B comparison of a known-good module against the loaded copy (NrthAuditDiff): reports only located functions whose state changed; "pattern absent from the other build" is separated from tampering
explicit_non_goals: no process access, no injection, no hooking, no memory writes
no Lua payload and no netc.dll check disable — those are the cheat, not the detector
no obfuscation/stealth/persistence code of any kind
audit_tool.validated: 30 unit tests + 21 self-test checks on the host; audit returns "0 with a match" on both samples (no self-flagging); sweep returns exactly the same 8 .data candidates as the independent Python tool; self-diff returns no delta. One command for all of it: run_all_tests.sh (8 passed, 0 failed)
audit_tool.artifacts_note: build_audit.sh normalises both binaries with tools/pe_deterministic.py (TimeDateStamp, CodeView PDB GUID, build id zeroed), so these SHA-256 values are reproducible for this toolchain; a different compiler version changes code bytes - then compare size + the 23 exports

tests.suite: bash recovered_or_reconstructed_project/run_all_tests.sh -> 9 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (8 + 1 skip when bin/ is absent)

audit_tool.diff_semantics: added_footprint (alert, = function return value) requires the footprint to sit on the function the baseline located at the same RVA; target_lost and sus_unlocated are other-build artefacts and never alert. Rule added in 1.2.0 after diffing the sample against this repository's own reconstruction produced a false DETOUR_JMP32 row on a jump thunk.
